data.name: Steam.Why

data.name: Steam.What

data.name: Backup.Title
data.value: Save your profile with the backup tool

data.name: Backup.Intro
data.value: The backup tool is a small Windows app that saves your profile (statistics, inventory, trophies, hunt history and more) as files on your PC while the official servers were still up, until 2026-11-11. It only reads; it changes nothing on the server.

data.name: Backup.Step1
data.value: Download backup-win-x64.zip and unpack it. Keep backup.exe and settings.json in the same folder.

data.name: Backup.Step2
data.value: Start backup.exe. For your own account, open the game and start a hunt (the backup tool can be open before or after); or choose "Public profile" and type a handle or id.

data.name: Backup.Step3
data.value: Tick what to save, press Start. The result is a backup folder and a backup zip in Documents\game-backup. Keep that backup zip private.

data.name: Backup.SmartScreen

data.value: em$ is {game}'s virtual currency that can be used to purchase items in the Store, such as weapons, equipment, clothing and much more.

data.name: Bank.Q2
data.value: How do I buy em$ as a gift to a friend?

data.name: Bank.A2
data.value: In the "Buy em$" tab of this window, check the "Purchase as a gift" check box and then click on the "BUY" button of the currency amount you wish to purchase. You will be taken to a purchase summary on the Steam website. Click on the "Authorize" button. You will be taken to a confirmation page (thank you for your purchase). Click on your em$ balance on the top of the screen (where it says "em$ XXXX") and check your {0}Purchase History{1}. The most recent entry in your Purchase History should read "Purchased as gift. Gift code:", followed by the gift code. Copy the code and send it to the friend you want to give it as a gift. Your friend will then have to redeem the code in order for the em$ gift to be added to their balance.

data.name: Bank.Q3
data.value: How do I redeem a gift code?

data.name: Bank.A3
data.value: Click on the "Redeem a discount code" button on the top-right corner of this window, then paste your gift code there and click on the "OK" button. A confirmation message will appear, click on the "Click here to redeem this gift" button. A message will appear confirming that your gift has been added to your account. Click OK and enjoy your gift!

data.name: Bank.A5
data.value: As with most digital currencies, we do not offer refunds for purchases of em$. The game is free to download and try out, please verify it does work on your computer and it is what you expect before purchasing em$.

data.name: Bank.A6
data.value: Please note that em$ cannot be sold or transferred, and cannot be exchanged for cash or anything else except for the actual {game} content. em$ are non-refundable. em$ have no monetary value and do not constitute currency or property of any type.

data.name: Help.Support.Ticket

data.name: Help.Guides.Text
data.value: {game} has a large community, check out some of these great resources created by our members.

data.name: Help.Tut.Intro
data.value: Learn the basics of how to play {game}. Make sure to go through the {0}playable tutorials{1} as well before going on your first hunt in the Evergreen Hunting Reserve!

data.name: Help.Community.Text
data.value: {game} has a vibrant community and many of our players hang out in local communities with players from their region! Check out these local {game} community fan sites!

data.name: DayHelp.Intro.1
data.value: Daily missions are a brand new addition to {game}'s mission system that can be found in the {0}Missions section{1} in the Launcher or Website.

data.name: DayHelp.Intro.2
data.value: As they are meant to be completed in one day, Daily Missions are supposed to be quite simple and most will not require specific weapons or equipment. Hard Daily Missions may sometimes be an exception to this, but don't be discouraged! You can complete Dailies in Multiplayer if you like.

data.name: DayHelp.How.1
data.value: Each day every player receives a new Daily Mission to complete. Different players will receive different Daily Missions (DM from now on).

data.name: DayHelp.How.2
data.value: Completing a DM increases your DM streak by 1. A {0}streak{1} is defined as a series of completed consecutive DMs.

data.name: DayHelp.How.3
data.value: Skipping or failing to complete a DM will "break your streak" and will bring you back to day one.

data.name: DayHelp.How.4
data.value: If you break your streak, Daily Missions will become inactive until you either Activate them to start a new streak or resume your last streak. A broken streak can be recovered using a {0}Resume Streak{1} service from the Store to continue from your last completed Daily Mission.

data.name: DayHelp.Diff.Intro
data.value: DMs come in three difficulty levels:

data.name: DayHelp.Diff.1
data.value: Each difficulty level is color-coded: an easy DM is represented by a green icon, a medium DM by a blue icon, and a hard DM by a red icon.

data.name: DayHelp.Diff.2
data.value: In addition to colors, each difficulty level has a different number of stars: 1 star for easy, 2 stars for medium, and 3 stars for hard.

data.name: DayHelp.Diff.3
data.value: Each difficulty level comes with different base rewards: {0}100 gm$ for Easy, 500 gm$ for Medium, and 1000 gm$ for Hard{1} respectively.

data.name: DayHelp.Diff.4
data.value: Rewards increase as your DMs streak gets longer, more on this below.

data.name: DayHelp.Prog.1
data.value: Your first DM will always be an easy one. If you complete it, DMs of different difficulty levels will alternate according to a pattern that we call a {0}cycle{1}.

data.name: DayHelp.Prog.3
data.value: As you can see a cycle lasts for 16 days, provided of course that you keep completing the DMs that are assigned to you day after day.

data.name: DayHelp.Prog.4
data.value: Once the first cycle is completed, a new cycle begins with {0}gm$ rewards increased by 10%{1} (Easy = 110 gm$, Medium = 550 gm$, Hard = 1100 gm$).

data.name: DayHelp.Prog.5
data.value: With every subsequent cycle, rewards increase by an extra 10% up to a maximum of double the amount of the base rewards (a 100% increase).

data.name: DayHelp.Prog.6
data.value: So for example, if you manage to complete 10 cycles in a row without breaking your streak you will then receive a x2 reward for each mission, which will continue until you break your streak.

data.name: DayHelp.Reg.1
data.value: Unlike regular missions, for a harvest to be valid in DMs, you will have to kill the animal yourself. Friends can still help you {0}find{1} the required animal in a Multiplayer session though.

data.name: DayHelp.Reg.2
data.value: Unlike regular missions, Daily Missions don't need to be activated. A Daily Mission is always active for the time it lasts (24 hours).

data.name: DayHelp.Ach.1
data.value: You can earn achievements by completing DMs. You can check your DM achievements in the Achievements section of your player's profile:

data.name: DayHelp.Ach.2
data.value: Completing DMs will count towards 3 different types of achievements, one for each difficulty level.

data.name: DayHelp.Ach.3
data.value: Here's a table showing the milestones for each difficulty level:

data.name: DayHelp.Rewards.1
data.value: As you progress through your DM streak you will receive special rewards for completing Hard (difficulty) DMs.

data.name: DayHelp.Rewards.2
data.value: Special rewards come in the form of:

data.name: DayHelp.Rewards.3
data.value: Items and trophies are exclusive rewards that you can win only by completing DMs (i.e. there's no other way to obtain them!). Your rewards will only show at the start of a new game.

data.name: DayHelp.Rewards.4
data.value: {0}IMPORTANT:{1} All of the DM's Special Rewards can only be won once! If you break your streak and start a new one, you will still receive gm$ but will need to surpass your previous streak to earn new Special rewards.

data.name: DayHelp.Rewards.5
data.value: You will be able to see any special rewards in the Rewards section of your DM:

data.name: DayHelp.Rewards.6
data.value: Here's a handy table showing how this works:

data.name: DayHelp.Rewards.Col.Streak
data.value: Number of Hard DMs completed in a row (streak)

data.name: DayHelp.Resume.1
data.value: As the name suggests, this service allows you to resume a DM's streak. For example, if you have a long streak of completed DMs and then missed or failed a DM, you can use this service to resume your streak and continue from your last completed DM.

data.name: DayHelp.Resume.2
data.value: The good thing is, it doesn't matter how much time has passed since you broke your streak, you will always be able to resume it - even if you broke it, say, a year before.

data.name: DayHelp.Resume.3
data.value: This service can be purchased in advance and activated when needed. There is no limit to how many of these cards you can purchase or own.

data.name: DayHelp.Resume.4
data.value: You can purchase this service directly on the DM page: as soon as you break your streak a button will appear to the left of your "Day 1" DM, prompting you to buy it (or use it, if you already own at least one).

data.name: DayHelp.Resume.5
data.value: Alternatively, you can purchase it from the {0}Store{1}.

data.name: DayHelp.Resume.6
data.value: Once purchased you will be able to use this service directly on the DM page:

data.name: Download.Title
data.value: How to play {game} on Hunter Resurgence

data.name: Download.Need.Text
data.value: A PC with Windows 10 or 11, Steam, and your own copy of {game} installed from your Steam library. Hunter Resurgence contains no game files: its launcher connects your copy to the community server.

data.name: Download.Installed
data.value: Already installed? Start Hunter Resurgence from the Start menu.

data.name: Download.Step1.Text
data.value: Download the Hunter Resurgence launcher and run it. It installs for your user only (no administrator prompt), adds a shortcut and updates itself.

data.name: Download.Restore.Title
data.value: Played before? Get your profile back

data.name: Download.Restore.Text
data.value: Sign in on this website and open {0}Restore your backup{1}. Have a backup zip? Upload it there: the operator checks it by hand, then restores it. No backup zip? Use “Claim your old profile” there with your old hunter name.

data.name: Download.Trouble.Guide
data.value: Player guide: every step, and fixes for common problems

data.name: Download.Step2.Text
data.value: On its first start, the launcher opens the setup window: choose Set up, and answer Yes when Windows asks to install a certificate and to edit the hosts file. Steam's Play button dialog follows at the next launcher start (or at once after “Not now”): choose “Close Steam and set it”. Steam starts again by itself. The game's files are never changed.

data.name: Download.Step3.Text
data.value: Press “Sign in with Steam” in the launcher and sign in in the browser that opens, with the Steam account you play with. Choose a reserve and a start, then press Start Game. The first time, Windows Firewall asks about the game: choose Allow. Keep the launcher open while you play.

data.name: Data.Intro
data.value: What this server keeps about you, and how to get rid of it.

data.name: Data.Stored.Steam
data.value: Your Steam id, the number Steam gives when you sign in. Nothing else of your Steam profile is kept.

data.name: Data.Stored.Handle
data.value: Your handle, the name other hunters see.

data.name: Data.Stored.Game
data.value: The game data of your account: inventory, wallet, skills, statistics, achievements, trophies, hunts, kills and the photos you take in the game.

data.name: Data.Stored.Zip
data.value: Each backup zip you upload, unchanged: kept for an operator to check, and after it is restored, so that the operator can reset your account and restore it again. A zip holds what the backup tool saved of your account.

data.name: Data.Stored.Sessions
data.value: Sign-in cookies and game tokens, as hashes that cannot be read back.

data.name: Data.Never.Text
data.value: Your e-mail address, real name, postal address or phone number: they are not asked for and not kept in your account. If a backup holds a field like that, it is not restored.

data.name: Data.Delete.Text
data.value: Sign in, open Restore your backup and use Delete my data. It deletes the account, its game data, the kept zips and the photos, and signs you out. Your Steam id is then forgotten, with two exceptions: it stays with the time of the deletion and nothing else for 24 hours (removed by the next daily cleanup), so that a new account cannot claim an old profile at once; and if the operator banned it, its ban record stays (see below). Signing in again makes a new account.

data.name: Data.Operator
data.value: The operator of this server can see all of the above.

data.name: Data.Reports.Launcher
data.value: After a game start fails (it ran under a minute, ended with an error, or showed no window), the launcher puts together a report: the game's logs and settings, the launcher's own log, Windows crash events for the game, the launcher and its browser (WebView2), the names of antivirus, booster and overlay programs, your Windows version and language, graphics card and screens, and your recent starts. Its text files hold no passwords or tokens. It is sent only if you chose "Send automatically" (asked once, changeable in Settings), otherwise only when you press Send. It is kept with your account for 30 days and the operators can read it. A notice with your handle, account number and the report's reference goes to the operators' private Discord channel. Delete my data removes your reports.

data.name: Data.Reports.Dump
data.value: A report can also hold the game's last crash dump, a copy of part of the game's memory at the crash. Unlike the rest of the report, it is not cleaned: it can hold what the game had in memory.

data.name: Data.Reports.Game
data.value: The game sends its own crash reports itself. The server keeps the crash and error ones for 30 days per account, with install paths and the device identifier removed.

data.name: Terms.Intro
data.value: Hunter Resurgence is a free, unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with the publisher of the game.

data.name: Terms.AsIs
data.value: The service is provided as it is, with no guarantee that it works, stays available or keeps your data.

data.name: Terms.Change
data.value: The service and its accounts can change or stop at any time.

data.name: Terms.Conduct.Text
data.value: Do not harass or insult other hunters, use another person's account, attack or overload the service, or upload a backup that is not yours.

data.name: Terms.Cheats
data.value: Do not use cheats, memory editing or modified game files.

data.name: Terms.Suspend
data.value: The operator may suspend accounts that break these rules.

data.name: Terms.Game
data.value: The game itself stays under its own license; these terms do not change it.

data.name: Terms.Data
data.value: How your data is handled is explained on the {0} page.

data.name: Data.Who.Text
data.value: Hunter Resurgence is a free fan project run by its operator. To reach the operator, write on the project's Discord server (link in the footer) or to contact@hunter-resurgence.com.

data.name: Data.Why.Text
data.value: Your data is used to run the service you ask for: sign-in, your account and restoring your backup. The operator also has a legitimate interest in keeping the service working and safe (logs, checking uploads). Nothing is sold or used for advertising.

data.name: Data.Keep.Account
data.value: Your account and its data stay until you use Delete my data.

data.name: Data.Keep.Logs
data.value: Server and proxy logs can contain IP addresses and handles. They are kept for at most 30 days.

data.name: Data.Keep.Steam
data.value: When an account is deleted, its Steam id and the time of the deletion are kept for 24 hours and then removed by the next daily cleanup. A ban by the operator is kept as a record of the Steam id, the time, the reason and, once lifted, the time it was lifted; the record stays after a lift, so that a later claim can show the Steam id was banned before, and it stays when the account is deleted.

data.name: Report.ErrSignIn
data.value: You are not signed in. Sign in again and try once more.

data.name: Report.ErrFormat
data.value: The community server did not accept the report.

data.name: Report.ErrSize
data.value: The report is too big to send. Save it instead.

data.name: Report.ErrLimit
data.value: A report is already on its way, or you sent five in the last 24 hours. Try again later.

data.name: Report.ErrDisk
data.value: The community server has no room for reports right now. Save the report instead.

data.name: Report.ErrSave
data.value: The report could not be saved to Downloads. Send it instead.

data.name: Report.ErrNetwork
data.value: The community server could not be reached. Try again, or save the report instead.
